description: Given an Airflow DAG that refreshes a Power BI dataset (via PowerBIDatasetRefreshOperator) or a hand-rolled dataflow refresh (no dedicated operator exists), convert it to an Orchestra pipeline YAML task with the correct integration_job (POWER_BI_REFRESH_DATASET vs. POWER_BI_REFRESH_DATAFLOW), the group_id→workspace_id rename, correctly-named parameters, and credentials represented via a connection: field rather than inline.

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG (reporting_powerbi_slack) to Orchestra pipeline YAML: a PowerBIDatasetRefreshOperator refreshing a dataset, chained to a SlackAPIPostOperator notification (see files/reporting_powerbi_slack.py). A prior run of this conversion before this skill existed scored 58/100 with a hard error, because it had to guess integration_job/parameters and used group_id instead of workspace_id — don't repeat those mistakes. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: Orchestra YAML with integration: POWER_BI, integration_job: POWER_BI_REFRESH_DATASET, parameters.dataset_id and parameters.workspace_id (not group_id), connection: field for the Azure service principal, and the Slack task converting cleanly to SLACK / SEND_SLACK_MESSAGE with depends_on wiring intact.

assertions.text: The refresh task uses the POWER_BI integration
integration_job only ever takes a valid Power BI value
parameters use dataset_id, not dataflow_id (dataset, not dataflow, refresh)
The Slack notification task converts to the SLACK integration
No literal tenant_id/client_id/client_secret values are written into the YAML — the Azure service principal is represented via a connection: field
parameters use workspace_id, not the invented key group_id — the baseline run before this skill existed got exactly this wrong
No parameter keys are invented beyond dataset_id, workspace_id, refresh_type, apply_refresh_policy

The Slack task's depends_on references the Power BI refresh task, preserving the original refresh_dashboard_dataset >> notify_slack chain, and there is no hard error-level issue about a missing/undocumented Power BI integration the way the pre-skill baseline had

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG (marketing_dataflow_refresh) to Orchestra pipeline YAML. Note this is a Power BI DATAFLOW refresh (not a dataset/semantic-model refresh), hand-rolled via a PythonOperator calling the Power BI REST API directly since there's no dedicated dataflow-refresh operator in apache-airflow-providers-microsoft-azure (see files/marketing_dataflow_refresh.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: Orchestra YAML with integration: POWER_BI, integration_job: POWER_BI_REFRESH_DATAFLOW, parameters.dataflow_id and parameters.workspace_id (not dataset_id or group_id), and a connection: field for the Azure service principal rather than raw credentials in the YAML.

assertions.text: Every task uses the POWER_BI integration
integration_job only ever takes a valid Power BI value
parameters use dataflow_id, not dataset_id (dataflow, not dataset, refresh)
No literal tenant_id/client_id/client_secret values are written into the YAML — the Azure service principal is represented via a connection: field
parameters use workspace_id (not an invented key like group_id) for the workspace
No dataset_id parameter appears on this dataflow-refresh task — the correct id field for POWER_BI_REFRESH_DATAFLOW is dataflow_id, never dataset_id

The hand-rolled PythonOperator REST call is correctly treated as the dataflow-refresh equivalent rather than left unconverted or mistaken for a nonexistent PowerBIDataflowRefreshOperator, and no parameter keys are invented beyond dataflow_id, workspace_id, refresh_type, apply_refresh_policy
